name: Brain Co.
summary: Brain Co. launched from stealth in September 2025 with a $30 million Series A to help large organisations adopt AI. The company describes its mandate broadly, and no valuation was announced with the round.
overview: Brain Co. is an enterprise-AI company that emerged from stealth in September 2025. It was incubated by Elad Gil, Jared Kushner, Luis Videgaray and Eric Wu, and aims to help large institutions incorporate AI into consequential operations.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Brain Co. announced the financing alongside its public launch; valuation was not announced.

bull_case: The company's backers and network could create access to large institutional customers at a moment when organisations are seeking practical AI adoption. A focused implementation platform could command high-value enterprise relationships if it establishes a clear product wedge.
bear_case: Public disclosure remains sparse on product, customers and commercial model. The profile should not be read as a brain-computer-interface thesis; the confirmed financing announcement describes enterprise AI adoption rather than a hardware neurotechnology business.

intelligence.description: An enterprise-AI company helping large institutions incorporate AI into their operations.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the September 2025 Series A

company: Brain Co. emerged from stealth in September 2025 with a $30 million Series A co-led by Gil Capital and Affinity Partners. Its stated mission is to help large organisations incorporate AI, with the company framed as a bridge between leading AI talent and major institutions.

The financing announcement named a broad group of technology and business leaders as participants but did not disclose a valuation, product revenue or detailed customer base. The profile therefore treats it as an early enterprise-AI platform rather than assigning a more specific category unsupported by public evidence.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Brain Co. is a useful watchlist case for the institutionalisation of AI adoption. The next evidence needed is a concrete product narrative, deployment outcomes and identifiable customer demand.

changed.text: Profile reviewed against available public information.

takeaways: The confirmed public category is enterprise AI, not brain-computer interfaces.
The $30M Series A was announced without a valuation.
Product specificity and customer evidence are the key missing diligence points.
